newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Former minister, nine others, on trial in S.Korea.
newsitem.headline: Former minister, nine others, on trial in S.Korea.

text.p: A former South Korean cabinet minister and the founder of the Hanbo Group went on trial on Monday over the collapse of the country's second-biggest steelmaker in a loans scandal.

They were among 10 defendants who appeared before a three-judge panel in a Seoul criminal court to face charges in connection with loans to Hanbo Steel Co, which collapsed in January under debts of $5.8 billion.
Former home affairs minister Kim Woo-suk has been charged with bribery and Hanbo founder Chung Tae-soo with fraud, issuing bad cheques and violating laws on trust and savings companies.
Also in the dock are three top bankers, four legislators -- three from the ruling party and one from the main opposition group -- and Chung's accountant.
They were dressed in pale blue prison uniforms with white rubber shoes.
